correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge3\) the crown distances give the exact \(0/2/1\) edge-coordinate formula. Two matched index-pairs omitted from a generator create an explicit indistinguishable edge pair, proving the \(n-1\) lower bound. A one-per-pair transversal outside one omitted pair decodes tail/head/neither at every represented index and therefore resolves all ordered edge-index pairs. The counting statement then follows by pigeonhole. The packaged exhaustive checker independently verifies the distance formula, all smaller subsets, and every minimum-size subset for \(3\le n\le8\).

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical symmetric family obtained by the minimal structured deletion of a perfect matching from \(K_{n,n}\). The theorem shows a large, exact sensitivity phenomenon: the edge metric dimension drops from \(2n-2\) to \(n-1\) after deleting only \(n\) edges, and it completely classifies and counts every optimum basis. This is a structural family theorem rather than a routine isolated computation.
